answer: We deploy dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect punishment matrices, an atlas of cryptoeconomic primitives where zero-knowledge verifiable delay locks staking collateral. Capital barrier analysis proves Sybil multiplication yields strictly negative expected attack utility, since the crystal threshold of slashing penalties annihilates revenue across the attacker's terrace of duplicated nodes. This cost asymmetry guarantees robust Nash equilibrium convergence, forcing rational adversaries to abandon attacks and accept intrinsic payoffs.
